questions.q: Where does the actual data behind a dashboard widget come from?
options: The dashboard stores its own copy of the data
A report that the widget is pointed at
A formula written directly in the widget
The object's page layout
questions.explain: A dashboard stores no data of its own. Every widget is backed by a real report, and the dashboard simply visualizes that report's results.

questions.q: What controls who can see a given dashboard?
options: The dashboard's own private sharing checkbox
The folder the dashboard is saved in, same as reports
Whoever created the underlying reports
Dashboards are always visible to the entire org
questions.explain: Dashboards follow the same folder-based sharing model as reports — the folder's sharing settings determine the audience.

questions.q: In the Dashboard Builder, what does the + Widget button do?
options: Deletes the currently selected widget
Opens the picker to add a new chart, metric, gauge, table, or text element
Changes the dashboard's folder
Refreshes all existing widgets
questions.explain: + Widget opens the add-widget flow, where you choose a widget type and the source report that will power it, then place it on the grid.

questions.q: A manager says a number on their dashboard looks wrong. Where should an admin actually investigate first?
options: The dashboard's color scheme
The underlying report the widget is pointed at
The user's browser cache only
The dashboard's folder sharing settings
questions.explain: Since a widget's number comes entirely from its source report, a wrong-looking number is almost always a report-level issue (filters, grouping, or data) rather than something in the dashboard itself.

questions.q: What happens to a dashboard widget if its underlying report's filters are changed?
options: Nothing — the widget keeps showing the old results until manually rebuilt
The widget automatically reflects the updated report the next time it refreshes
The widget is deleted automatically
The dashboard must be entirely rebuilt from scratch
questions.explain: Because widgets are live pointers to their source reports, changing the report updates every widget and dashboard built on it the next time it refreshes — no manual rebuild needed.
